verses.text: A song of ascents. LORD, remember David and all the hardship he went through.
Remember how he swore to the LORD and made a vow to the Mighty One of Jacob:
“I won’t go inside my house or climb into my bed.
I won’t let my eyes close in sleep or even let my eyelids doze
until I find a place for the LORD, a home for the Mighty One of Jacob.”
Look, we heard about it in Ephrathah and found it in the fields of Jaar.
“Let’s go into his home. Let’s worship at his footstool.”
Rise up, LORD, and go into your resting place, you and the ark of your strength.
Let your priests wear righteousness like clothing. Let your holy people shout with joy!
For the sake of David your servant, don’t turn your anointed one away.
The LORD swore David a true oath. He won’t take it back: “I’ll put one of your own children on your throne.
If your children keep my covenant and the testimony I teach them, their children will sit on your throne forever too.”
The LORD chose Zion. He wanted to make it his home.
“This is my resting place forever. I’ll live here, because this is where I want to be.
I’ll give her plenty of supplies and fill her poor with bread.
I’ll dress her priests in salvation, and her holy people will shout for joy.
There I’ll make David’s horn grow strong. I’ve set up a lamp for my anointed one.
I’ll dress his enemies in shame, but the crown on his own head will shine.”
